section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Toldos,
Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5727

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the verse mentions both finding a hundredfold and being blessed by G-d, implying they are separate matters, and asks what the unspecified blessing was.
section.t: "And Yitzchak sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and G-d blessed him."
And it needs to be understood,
From the fact that it says "and G-d blessed him" after "he found... a hundredfold,"
it implies that "and G-d blessed him" is an additional matter beyond his finding a hundredfold,
and an explanation is needed as to why it says "and He blessed him" without specifying with what He blessed him.
Also, it needs to be understood,
Behold, even this finding of a hundredfold
(one hundred times what was estimated)
is not according to the ways of nature, but rather the blessing of G-d,
and on the other hand,
also the blessing of "and G-d blessed him" that came after the finding of the hundredfold is that Yitzchak was blessed with this blessing
("and G-d blessed him"),
and nevertheless, the finding of the hundredfold is attributed by the verse to Yitzchak
("and he found... a hundredfold"),
and regarding the blessing with which Yitzchak was blessed after he found the hundredfold, it says "and G-d blessed him."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects in the verse—finding a hundredfold and being blessed—relate to the produce, while the subsequent verse about Yitzchak growing great refers to his entire being.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what the verse continues,
"And the man grew great, and he went on growing until he became very great,"
that through "and Yitzchak sowed, etc." there was a growth in Yitzchak himself,
"and the man grew great, etc."
For the two matters in the verse "and Yitzchak sowed, etc.,"
"and he found... a hundredfold" and "and G-d blessed him,"
are regarding the produce,
"and he found a hundredfold" is an extraordinary increase in the produce itself,
"and G-d blessed him" is that he sold his produce at a high price.
And although all matters of the Patriarchs
[and particularly the matters of the Patriarchs mentioned in the Torah]
are spiritual matters,
from this it is understood that in Yitzchak's produce there was
(also)
a spiritual matter,
and the two matters of "and he found a hundredfold" and "and G-d blessed him" are also regarding the spiritual aspect of Yitzchak's produce,
nevertheless,
they are only regarding a particular matter
(produce).
And in the subsequent verse it adds that through the service of "and Yitzchak sowed, etc." there was also growth in his entire being,
"and the man grew great, etc."
